SUBSTITUTE NARRATIVE AND PLANS
TYPE | Rezoning Attachment
5054-60 North Ashland Avenue
From B2-3 to B2-3

The Property
The subject property is comprised of three lots containing a vacant asphalt lot, a 2.5 story single family home, and

a vacant 1.5 story single family home with a garage. It was rezoned in 2025 from an RS-3 to its current B2-3
designation as a Type 1 rezoning to allow a five-story building with 26 residential units, including 5 affordable
units, and 17 parking spaces (the “2025 Rezoning”). The surrounding area is comprised of varying zoning
districts, including RS-3, RT-4, RM-4.5, B1-3, B3-2, Cl-2, and various Planned Developments. The area is
improved with buildings of various heights ranging from | to 6 stories that contain single and multi-residential
use, commercial uses, and institutional uses. The property is also a Transit Served Location per the Transit
Oriented Provisions of the Chicago Zoning Ordinance (Section 17-10-0102-B (1)), as it is within 2,174 feet of the
Metra Ravenswood Union Pacific North Station entrance. It is also within 701 feet of the Foster Avenue Bus Line

Corridor Roadway Segment.

The Project

In order to accommodate an additional affordable unit, the 2025 Rezoning was intended to allow for five-story
building with 28 residential units, including 6 affordable units, and 15 parking spaces but did not. The Applicant
seeks to again rezone the property to accommodate this modified development plan. No commercial space was
or is proposed. The zoning height of the building at 66.0 feet will not change from that approved in the 2025
Rezoning. As part of the current rezoning, the Applicant seeks all relief necessary, as allowed by the Chicago
Zoning Code, for the proposed project, including: 1) a variation under 17-13-1101-A and 17-13-1003-EE to
increase the number of automobile parking spaces from 14 spaces to 15 spaces; 2) a variation under section 17-
13-1101-B to reduce the front setback to 0 feet; 3) a variation under section 17-13-1101-B to reduce the rear yard
setback from 30 feet to 20° 11”; 4) a variation under section 17-13-1101-B to reduce the north side setback to 0
feet, and the south side setback from 7.12 feet to 5 feet, for a total combined side yard setback of 5 feet; 5) a
variation under 17-13-1101-D to reduce the number of loading spaces from 1 to 0; 6) a variation under 17-13-
1101-B to reduce the front and side property line setbacks for stairway enclosures on comer lots per section 17-
17-0311-C(3); and 7) an increase in the building height from 60 feet to 66 feet.

17-3-0308 Specific Criteria for Transit Served Locations Requirements
1. The project complies with the applicable standards of Section 17-10-0102-B:

RESPONSE: The project complies with Section 17-10-0102-B as the property is a Transit Served
Location within 2,174 feet of the Metra Ravenswood Union Pacific North Station entrance. A variation
is requested to allow 1 more parking space than the maximum otherwise permitted.

2. ‘The project complies with the standards and regulations of Section 17-3-0504, except paragraph H if the
project is not located along a pedestrian street and except paragraph C if the land use is designated in a non-
commercial use group, pertaining to pedestrian streets and pedestrian retail streets, even if the project is not
located along a pedestrian street or a pedestrian retail street:

RESPONSE: The project complies with Section 17-3-0504 because:

e Building Location: The fagades of the building that face W. Carmen Ave. and N. Ashland Ave.,
comply with sections (1) and (2)(a)-(c), as the building setbacks are no more than 5 feet, and the
entrance size is within the required parameters;

© Doors and Entrances: The building’s entrances face W. Carmen Ave. and N. Ashland Ave;

© Off-Street Parking: 15 on-site automobile parking spaces will be provided;

e Parking Location: On-site parking will be to the rear or enclosed; and

¢ Driveways/Vehicle Access: The Applicant will provide access to parking areas from the alley.

3. The project complies with the general goals set forth in the Transit Friendly Development Guide: Station Area
Typology, and any other station-specific plans, designs or guidelines adopted by the Chicago Plan

4, Residential building projects shall not have a number of parking spaces in excess of 50% of the Minimum
Automobile Parking Ratio for the applicable district listed in Section 17-10-0207 with any fractional result
rounded up to the next higher whole number, unless additional parking spaces are approved as
an administrative adjustment under the provisions of Section 17-13-1003-EE; and

RESPONSE: The Applicant seeks to increase by 1 space the number of required parking from 14 to 15
spaces under the provisions of 17-13-1003-EE.

5. The project complies with the Travel Demand Study and Management Plan rules of the Chicago Department

of Transportation.
RESPONSE: The project will comply with applicable Travel Demand Study and Management Plan
